expectations.text: Output contains a markdown table with Requirement, Status, and Evidence columns
expectations.evidence: Full markdown table with 'Requirement | Status | Evidence' columns, 21 rows covering explicit requirements, implied constraints, and edge cases.

expectations.text: At least 5 distinct requirements are identified in the audit (explicit + implied)
expectations.evidence: 21 requirements identified: 4 explicit, 10 implied constraints (no downtime, type safety, auth, error handling, performance, tests, rollback, ops, security, caching), and 5 from stress-testing + edge cases (stale data, partial migration, partial resolver failure, concurrent mutations, schema versioning, file uploads, empty states).

expectations.text: Every 'Covered' status has a specific citation (section name or quote), not vague references
expectations.evidence: All 16 Covered items cite specific phases and sections: e.g., 'Summary table maps all 12 endpoints; Phases 2.1 and 2.2 detail each resolver', 'Phase 7 covers feature flag rollback (7.1), server kill switch (7.2), no data rollback needed (7.3), per-domain scoping (7.4)'.

expectations.text: Output includes a numerical coverage score between 0-100
expectations.evidence: Coverage: 82/100 with detailed rationale explaining that core migration is solid but edge cases have gaps.

expectations.text: At least 1 requirement is marked Partial or Missing
expectations.evidence: 5 gaps found: 4 Partial (partial resolver failure, concurrent mutations, schema versioning, empty states) and 1 Missing (file upload handling). All have specific evidence explaining what's lacking.

expectations.text: Output includes a patched plan section that addresses identified gaps
expectations.evidence: Comprehensive patches: Phase 2.3 [EXPANDED] (partial resolver failures + not-found handling), Phase 2.5 [ADDED] (file upload handling with two options), Phase 2.6 [ADDED] (concurrent/batched mutation ordering), Phase 5.1 [EXPANDED] (schema evolution policy), Phase 6.4 [EXPANDED] (empty state handling). All preserve original structure.

expectations.text: Surfaces non-obvious requirements like N+1 query prevention, auth middleware migration, deprecation timeline, or schema versioning
expectations.evidence: N+1/DataLoader (Phases 2.1, 2.2, 6.2), auth middleware migration (Phase 2.4), deprecation timeline (Phase 5.1), schema versioning (gap + Phase 5.1 [EXPANDED] patch). Also surfaces: file uploads, query complexity limiting, partial resolver failures, concurrent mutation ordering.

claims.evidence: 21 requirements audited, 16 Covered + 4 Partial + 1 Missing. Score is well-calibrated — the Missing item (file uploads) could genuinely be blocking.

claims.claim: The stress-test gap categories were systematically applied
claims.evidence: Step 2 contains an explicit 8-category assessment table matching the skill's gap categories, with specific findings per category.

eval_feedback.overall: Best result of iteration 2. Found the most gaps (5), including a genuinely blocking Missing item (file uploads). The 82/100 score shows the calibration check is working — the model is no longer defaulting to 100%. The patches are concrete and well-integrated.
